text:
marta (sec-eng): noticed a cluster of KMS decrypt alerts from the same service account starting ~10:02 UTC, looks like a sudden spike :eyes:
alert-bot: [AUTO] KMS_DECRYPT_FAILURE x80 in 5m from service=repo-sync region=eu-west-1 key_id=redwood-prod-1
marta (sec-eng): hitting SIEM, tagging for triage. can we confirm whether RBAC changes deployed earlier could cause retries?
jake (oncall): looking. there was an RBAC allow change for service accounts in the deploy at 09:58 — might be related. I'll pull audit logs.
sam (sre): I see retries in the app logs, stack shows DecryptError -> retry loop. sample: `2026-04-05T09:59:14Z repo-sync svc=repo-sync pid=234 decrypt_error: AccessDenied`
olivia (product-security): @marta is this impacting customers? any data exfil concerns?
marta (sec-eng): no customer-facing errors reported so far, just internal job failures. low blast radius for now.
henry (audit): pulled KMS CloudTrail entries — same principal arn:aws:sts::1111:assumed-role/repo-sync-role. There are many AccessDenied events then successful Decrypt later from different principal.
jake (oncall): rolling back the RBAC change to previous policy now. will monitor.
alert-bot: [DEPLOY] rollback/repo-sync-policy applied by jake at 10:04 UTC
marta (sec-eng): good. for SIEM: this looks like a predictable FP pattern when a CI job rotates creds -> temporary AccessDenied bursts. we should avoid alert floods.
sam (sre): agreed. current SIEM rule is too trigger-happy: `WHEN count(kms.decrypt.failure) > 10 / 5m AND distinct_principals < 3` — bad for churny service accounts.
marta (sec-eng): proposal: add correlation with recent IAM policy-change events and with source.ip diversity. new rule idea:
```
WHEN count(kms.decrypt.failure) > 20 / 5m
AND NOT exists(iam.policy.change within 5m of first_event)
AND (distinct_principals > 1 OR distinct_regions > 1)
THEN alert severity = high
ELSE auto-suppress with summary
```
sam (sre): also add cooldown per principal and ignore retries coming from the same request-id prefix for 2m.
jake (oncall): practical quick fix: create a suppression window for repo-sync principal for 15m while we verify.
henry (audit): need to keep audit trail even if we suppress alerts. recommend routing suppressed events to a low-priority dashboard and retain full logs.
marta (sec-eng): agreed — suppressed vs dropped distinction important. add a 'suppressed-archive' index.
olivia (product-security): for comms: I'll draft a short blurb for infra->product channels: what happened, impact, mitigation, next steps.
marta (sec-eng): post-incident actions: 1) tune rule as above, 2) add IAM change correlation in SIEM, 3) add dashboard panel for KMS decrypt spikes with principal heatmap, 4) update runbook note about credential rotation patterns, 5) confirm no cross-region key usage.
sam (sre): I'll open a follow-up ticket with PR to SIEM rule + dashboard widgets. tag: #security-siem, assign to marta + sam.
jake (oncall): monitoring looks stable after rollback, error rate down to baseline at 10:12 UTC.
alert-bot: [INCIDENT] resolved (low) — 10:14 UTC
marta (sec-eng): thanks everyone. next step: schedule 30m working session tomorrow to implement rule changes and dashboard.
olivia (product-security): adding comms note to drafts, will ping for review.
henry (audit): I'll verify CloudTrail retention and ensure suppressed logs are accessible for future audits.
marta (sec-eng): closing thread; will post postmortem link when ticket created.
